correctness.rationale: A stationary state exists by finite-dimensional time averaging. Its support must be invariant under every jump (take the stationary equation on its kernel); the four nonzero local raising/lowering jumps generate the full matrix algebra, hence it is faithful. The adjoint fixed-point dissipation identity, traced against this state, forces every fixed observable to commute with every jump, so only scalars are fixed and the trace-one stationary state is unique. Phase covariance gives the stated X form. Independent exact replay with python3 /workspace/checks/qubit_algebra.py confirmed the generator equations, signs for c=ρ_10,01, and the concurrence polynomial and complementary-bath factorization. Solving gives z=(1+t²)⁻¹, c=2iJdz/(κ+iΔ) and the two extremal populations q²−d²z,(1−q)²−d²z, both positive under the strict occupation bounds. Thus the sign is that of F(z)=−h²+2d²(1−h)z−d²(1+d²)z². When d≠0 the maximizer is strictly inside (0,1), and both end values are negative. Its maximum is positive iff d²(1−2h)>h². Equality gives zero rather than positive concurrence. The strictly decreasing bijection from t≥0 to z∈(0,1] maps the two roots to the asserted finite open interval. At q=1/2 the inequality reduces to t²−2|m|t+1−m²<0, with the claimed roots and width. The result quantifies existence over J, not positivity at every J. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Set γ_j^+=κp_j, γ_j^−=κ(1−p_j), and x=4g²/(κ²+δ²). The prior expressions give (1+x)r_1=q²x+p_1p_2, (1+x)r_4=(1−q)²x+(1−p_1)(1−p_2), and (1+x)|c|=|d|√x. With D=d² the prior inequality is −h²x²+[2D(1−h)−2h²]x−[(q²−D)((1−q)²−D)]>0. Its discriminant is 4D[D(1−2h)−h²].

For D>0, positive discriminant implies positive sum of the roots; their product is positive under strict occupations. Thus the two positive roots give precisely the same interval in t=√x. For q=1/2 one has r_1=r_4, and taking the square root of the prior inequality immediately gives t²−2|m|t+1−m²<0.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The elimination is a direct quadratic discriminant calculation on previously supplied populations and entanglement sign, not a new bound or stronger feasibility theorem. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For two qubits positivity of either entanglement measure agrees; in this X form both criteria see exactly the coherence and the two extremal populations. The Khandelwal formulas are algebraic in the γ_j^± and the generator is the same for fixed positive jump rates, regardless of which bath statistics realizes them.

originality.rationale: The exact local detuned exchange Lindbladian, general rate-symbol stationary X-state, and exact entanglement criterion were already given by Khandelwal et al. (2020). After imposing equal total rates the claimed condition and entire coupling interval are the discriminant and positive-root interval of a quadratic directly in those displayed formulas. The inverted fermionic realization in Brask et al. corroborates the resonant model for occupations above one half; it is not necessary to identify the formal Lindblad rates with physical positive-temperature bosonic rates. The earlier authors did not need to state the boundary in (q,d) coordinates for the implication to hold.
residual_risks: The comparison is not a global historical priority determination. Khandelwal et al.'s bosonic physical realization is narrower in occupations than the frozen abstract rate model; the demonstrated coverage is an algebraic implication of their rate-symbol formulas for the identical generator, not a claim that a positive-temperature bosonic bath realizes inverted occupations.

value.rationale: The explicit occupation coordinates and bounded window are convenient, and the derivation is correct, but the central feasibility result is a one-variable discriminant test of the prior exact stationary state and positivity criterion. The complementary-bath width is a further direct simplification. The record does not establish a substantive uncovered result beyond this reparameterization and elimination.
